note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md (2026-11-27): 13 pictures chosen from 26 trial pictures. Wide pictures only (1920x1088). Each scene starts at the first word of its verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper 60% of the frame, clear of the word box. God is not pictured; Abram, Sarai, Lot and the others are only ordinary people of today, seen from behind or small. Fixed recurring objects: Abram's tent is a small plain weathered tan canvas tent on a simple wooden pole frame; the altar is a small altar of stacked rough fieldstones; the oak is one huge old oak with a broad gnarled trunk and a wide dark-green crown.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning; (2) write picture ideas for each; (3) judge them; (4) make the top two for each slot as real pictures and choose by eye.

sections.meaning: Abram comes back up from Egypt, rich in everything, to the first tent place and the first altar at Bethel.
Abram and Lot cannot share the land; Abram lets Lot choose, and Lot takes the well-watered plain and moves toward evil Sodom.
Yahweh tells Abram to look in every direction: all the land is his offspring's, as countless as dust; Abram settles at Mamre and builds an altar.

scenes.principle: And Abram went up from Egypt, he and his wife and all that he had, and Lot with him, to the Negev.
scenes.shows: Pack donkeys and a flock climb out of pale desert scrub onto a green ridge at dawn.
scenes.prompt: From behind, a line of loaded pack donkeys, a flock of sheep and a few walkers climbing from pale dry desert scrub up onto a green hill ridge at dawn, green hills opening ahead, warm low light. The animals and the ridge are in the upper part of the frame. The subject and every important detail are in the upper part of the frame.  The important part is in the upper half of the picture; the lower part is plain foreground.
